Interpretation with SLOOS overlay:
- Policy stance: The Committee kept the target range at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent and continues balance-sheet runoff, emphasizing data dependence and “balanced” risks. Growth remains solid, unemployment low, and inflation “somewhat elevated,” supporting a patient, restrictive stance.
- SLOOS signal: The latest SLOOS points to tighter credit supply across C&I and CRE lending, with banks citing the economic outlook, industry-specific problems, and reduced risk tolerance. Banks also report higher minimum credit score requirements for consumer loans and expect higher delinquencies and charge-offs. Demand appears mixed: some firmness in consumer categories (credit cards, autos) but softer on the business side, particularly weighing on smaller firms. 
- Implications: Tighter standards and expected credit deterioration introduce headwinds to growth and reinforce caution, offsetting part of the solid-activity tone and aligning with the Committee’s “balanced risks.” Financial stability concerns (CRE stress pockets, elevated asset valuations, run‑prone funding) further argue for patience.

Bottom line: Neutral with only a faint positive tilt from current activity; SLOOS tightness tempers the prior tone.
